artworks.title: The Sea Serpent
artworks.artist: Stephen Alonzo Schoff, after Elihu Vedder
artworks.medium: etching in black on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mr. S.R. Koehler, Boston, Massachusetts, 1881)
artworks.description: The image depicts a landscape with sandy dunes stretching towards the horizon, a low horizon line, an expansive sky with horizontal lines for texture, sparse vegetation and sandy surfaces, a winding pathway, and a monochrome color palette emphasizing contrast and depth through line density.

artworks.title: The Voyage of Life: Youth
artworks.medium: engraving in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image shows a river leading from a lush bank with various plants towards a distant temple-like structure with an orb on top. Detailed brushstrokes depict textures of trees, water, and mountains, creating depth. The color scheme is dominated by earthy tones and sepia hues, enhancing the serene atmosphere. A figure in white stands near the riverbank among the trees.

artworks.title: The Voyage of Life: Manhood
artworks.medium: engraving in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection

artworks.title: The Voyage of Life: Old Age
artworks.medium: engraving in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection

artworks.title: A Bit on Marblehead Neck
artworks.medium: etching in black on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of Frank B. Bristow, 1968)
artworks.description: The image depicts a pastoral landscape. There are grazing sheep, rocks, and low trees in the foreground. Rolling hills lead to a body of water in the distance, with a landmass beyond. The sky is filled with textured clouds. The landscape is created using fine, detailed linework and a monochromatic sepia color palette.

artworks.title: Up the Hill
artworks.medium: etching in black on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of Frank B. Bristow, 1968)
artworks.description: The image depicts a ground-level view of a rural scene with a path winding through trees. The horizon shows silhouettes of distant figures. Detailed etching techniques are used, creating a monochromatic palette of blacks, grays, and whites that emphasize texture and contrast.

artworks.title: Up the Hill
artworks.medium: etching in black on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mr. S.R. Koehler, Boston, Massachusetts, 1881)
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape scene with a pathway leading into the distance. The horizon is high in the composition with a line of trees diminishing in size. The path curves slightly and is bordered by a stone wall on the left and a wooden fence on the right. Trees fill the sides, with branches extending upwards. The artwork features detailed brushstrokes and etching marks creating texture. The color palette is monochromatic in shades of sepia and dark brown. In the distance, two figures are walking down the path.

artworks.title: A Lady of Cairo Visiting
artworks.artist: James David Smillie, after Frederic Arthur Bridgman
artworks.medium: etching in black on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mr. S.R. Koehler, Boston, Massachusetts, 1881)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a street scene in front of an elaborately decorated building. The scene depicts architectural details and natural elements surrounding the figures. In the image, a white donkey stands on the left with its tack accentuated. Next to a detailed arched doorway, there are two people cloaked in long robes; one is leaning against the building while another is seated on the ground with bowls. The stone building features carvings around the doorframe and latticework on its balconies and windows. The shading and crosshatching techniques bring out the textures of stone and fabric, casting a warm glow over the scene.

artworks.title: Landscape with Sheep
artworks.artist: James David Smillie, after Charles Émile Jacque
artworks.medium: etching in black on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mr. S.R. Koehler, Boston, Massachusetts, 1881)
artworks.description: The image shows a pastoral scene with a group of sheep in the center. The scenery includes a textured sky and trees. The artistic technique used is etching with detailed lines. The color palette is primarily earthy and muted tones. A figure sits under trees on the right side. In the distance, there are densely packed trees.

artworks.title: The Rocky Mountains
artworks.medium: steel engraving in black with chine collé on paperboard
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection

artworks.title: A Song of Parting to the Boy He Sung
artworks.artist: Lumb Stocks, after George Elgar Hicks
artworks.medium: engraving in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: There are three figures depicted in a line drawing. The first figure on the left is a man seated on a bed, with his right arm raised. He is shirtless, wearing traditional attire, including a feathered headdress. Next to him is a seated figure facing slightly away, wearing a draped garment. The third figure is lying in the bed, covered with bedding and asleep. The background shows a room with wooden wall panels, a window on the left, and firearms mounted on the right wall.

artworks.title: Mute, Gazing, Agonizing...
artworks.artist: Lumb Stocks, after George Elgar Hicks
artworks.medium: engraving in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: This is a drawing of several figures in a scene. The figures have varied poses and are depicted in a minimalistic and linear style. Some figures are holding spears, one is kneeling, and two are lying down. They are dressed in attire resembling historical or medieval clothing, suggesting a historical setting. The drawing portrays a moment of drama and tension, with one central figure reaching out and others observing.

artworks.title: The Burning of the Theatre in Richmond, Virginia
artworks.medium: hand-colored etching and aquatint on wove paper mounted to heavy wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Mary E. Maxwell Fund, 1956)
artworks.description: This is a painting of a theater fire. The image depicts a scene of chaos and flames as a building labeled as a theater is engulfed in fire. The fire consumes the structure, with large flames and smoke billowing into the sky. The foreground of the image shows a crowd amidst the blaze. The composition and style suggest an approach to capturing catastrophic events with detailed figures and lighting. This is in the style of historical engravings or lithographs from the early 19th century, often used to document significant events of the time.

artworks.title: Une petite séance a la buvette
artworks.medium: lithograph
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring two satirical scenes. In the top scene, two figures are at a buffet table with various food items, while a third figure sits at a small table in the background. The characters are exaggerated in their features, suggesting a caricature style. The lower scene shows an individual exiting a carriage with a grumpy expression and a small vehicle. The drawing captures the absurdity and humor associated with formal assemblies and their attendees using caricature to highlight the quirks and details of the characters and setting.

artworks.title: L'intérim d'un instituteur suspen du ...
artworks.medium: lithograph
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: This is an image of a soldier sitting at a desk instructing children. A soldier with a tall hat sits behind a desk, looking towards a group of seated children. Papers and an inkwell are on the desk.

artworks.title: La note ou la vie
artworks.medium: lithograph
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a debt collector presenting a bill to three figures. The scene includes a man in unique attire handing a bill to three figures in different clothing. The background features ships on water and architectural forms. Annotations and newspaper print are faintly visible in the background. The drawing is a caricature style, often used for satirical and political commentary.

artworks.title: War Sketches in the Capital
artworks.medium: hand-colored wood engraving on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, William A. Clark Fund, 1976)
artworks.description: This is a drawing depicting a large compound with various activities and structures. The central panel shows a building labeled "Cocoran's Private Clothing Dept. and Art Building" surrounded by figures on horseback and people using carriages. Other panels show scenes of a field with horses, workers handling bags, and natural landscapes with trees and a cylindrical tower. The illustration style is typical of the 19th century.

artworks.title: Landscape with Fallen Tree
artworks.medium: etching in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape with an old, gnarled tree in the center. The land slopes away from the tree, leading towards a horizon where a castle can be seen among rolling hills. The artwork appears to be an intricate etching, with delicate lines and textures created through crosshatching and varying line densities. The color scheme is monochromatic, using blacks and grays for contrast and texture. The scene includes a lush valley with dense vegetation and hills in the background under a sky marked with horizontal lines, indicating clouds.

artworks.title: Landscape with Hay Wagon
artworks.medium: etching and roulette in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: This image shows a riverside scene with tall trees reflecting in the calm water. The riverbank has various plants. In the background, a cart pulled by two oxen can be seen. The sky is cloudy. The artwork is done in an etching style with fine lines and cross-hatching, creating a detailed landscape. The color palette is dark sepia.

artworks.title: West View of Mount Vernon Mansion
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Mary E. Maxwell Fund, 1960)
artworks.description: The image displays a frontal view of Mount Vernon Mansion. The viewpoint is slightly elevated, capturing the mansion's architectural layout and surroundings. The mansion is centrally positioned and has a symmetrical design with a central cupola and columns at the entrance. Trees flank the house on both sides. The image shows a print or engraving technique, resulting in crisp lines delineating architectural details. The color palette is muted with soft greens, creams, and light blues. Small figures are visible on the lawn area, and the mansion serves as the focal point, with its light-colored façade contrasting the dark green shutters.

artworks.title: East View of Mount Vernon Mansion
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Mary E. Maxwell Fund, 1960)
artworks.description: The image shows an elevated view of the Mount Vernon Mansion. The horizon line is in the middle, dividing the foreground from the sky. The mansion is in the center, displaying its grand architecture. The brushstroke technique is precise and detailed. The color palette includes greens, browns, and creams. There is a grassy area in the foreground with figures and a dog. Trees frame the buildings, and the sky transitions from light blue to beige with white clouds.

artworks.title: Les Parisiens dans l'attente de le ...
artworks.medium: lithograph
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts several full-body figures standing upright outdoors, tilting their heads back and gazing upwards. In the foreground, a man and woman are prominently displayed. The man has an elongated face, a prominent nose, a tall hat, a long coat, a scarf or cravat, and holds an object under his arm. The woman has round facial features, an upturned nose, dark hair pulled back, a voluminous garment, a scarf or high collar, and holds her arms close to her chest. Behind them are two more figures in similar outdoor attire, also looking upwards. The background shows a cityscape with indistinct buildings against a dark, starry sky.

artworks.title: Youths and a Horse
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of J. William Middendorf, II, 1977)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures interacting with a horse. The illustration is rendered in fine black and white with delicate shading and detailing. It depicts one figure seated on the horse while another figure is standing beside, engaged in an interaction with the horse. The horse stands alert and steady, its posture and musculature detailed. The background is minimally rendered, focusing the viewer's attention on the interaction between the figures and the horse.

artworks.title: Herd of Cattle
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of J. William Middendorf, II, 1977)
artworks.description: The image shows a group of cows resting on the ground. Three cows are in the foreground, with two lying down and one standing. In the background, there is a smaller group of cows. The horizon is low and there are minimal landscape details. The drawing is done in pencil with delicate strokes, giving texture to the cows and surroundings. The closest cow is shaded darker for contrast. The color palette is monochromatic with soft grays on aged paper.
